content: Colesevelam is a medication prescribed to help lower cholesterol and certain fatty substances in the blood. It is used in conjunction with dietary changes, such as reducing cholesterol and fat intake, and regular exercise. This medication works by binding to bile acids in the intestines. Bile acids are produced when cholesterol is broken down in the body. By removing these bile acids, colesevelam helps to reduce blood cholesterol levels. High cholesterol and fat levels can lead to the buildup of these substances along the walls of arteries, a condition called atherosclerosis. This process reduces blood flow and oxygen delivery to vital organs like the heart and brain. Lowering cholesterol and fat levels in the blood can help prevent cardiovascular diseases, including heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Colesevelam can be used alone or in combination with other cholesterol-lowering medications, such as statins (e.g., atorvastatin, cerivastatin, lovastatin, pravastatin, or simvastatin). In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Colesevelam is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually once or twice daily with meals and a liquid. Your doctor will determine the appropriate dosage for you. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take colesevelam exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. You may notice a reduction in your lipid levels within two weeks of starting the medication. However, colesevelam does not cure high cholesterol, so you should continue taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking colesevelam without consulting your doctor. Before starting colesevelam, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to colesevelam or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including sustained-release formulations of verapamil (Calan SR), vitamins, and herbal products. Notify your doctor if you have a history of gastrointestinal issues, such as bowel obstruction or difficulty swallowing, triglyceride levels above 300 mg/dL, bleeding disorders, or low levels of fat-soluble vitamins (A, E, and K). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking colesevelam, contact your doctor immediately. While taking colesevelam, it is essential to follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This diet should include foods such as cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (except cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of colesevelam, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Colesevelam may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: gas, constipation, upset stomach, headache, weakness, muscle pain, or throat infection. Store colesevelam in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. It is important to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests to monitor your response to colesevelam. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Colesevelam is sold under the brand name WelChol®.
